title: Morphology of the warts of Graneledone pacifica and Pareledone charcoti (Cephalopoda: Megaleledonidae)
content: Octopod skin is renowned for its remarkable abilities to change colour and texture. Allen et al. (2014) detail how muscles within the skin generate the dynamic skin sculpture characteristic of shallow-water octopods. However, the skin texture of some octopods is characterized by seemingly permanent, spiny warts and limited ability to change colour (Voight, 2008). The skin of most species of the Megaleledonidae, Southern Ocean and deep-sea taxa with one row of arm suckers (Strugnell et al., 2014), is studded with either warts or papillae, except for that of M icroeledone mangoldii  Norman, Hochberg and Boucher-Rodoni, 2004 and, following Allcock (2005), three species of Pareledone Robson, 1932. The vast majority of these species live below the photic zone, in perpetual darkness. The nature and potential homologies of the structures in their skin are unexplored.
